conclusion: No earlier complete answer to the full inspected QC-GHP corrected counting target was identified in this bounded search. Mathematical novelty, method novelty, and formalization priority remain unestablished.

existing_results.comparison: Girth-eight cubic classification gives only (4,4) on four variables, so the requested (4,2) count is zero in the old scope.
no_four_two_error_bound concerns two-error syndrome weight, not (4,2) absorbing-set enumeration.

sources.title: Spectral and Additive Combinatorial Methods for Cycles and Absorbing Sets in Lifted-Product Quantum LDPC Codes
sources.relationship: Poses the deferred (4,2)/(4,0) counting task. The new formula retains actual incidences; the equal-M_j counterexample obstructs an M_j-only answer to the (4,2) component.
sources.comparison_limit: The joint canonical (4,2)/(4,0) target is only partially addressed. General incidence, cyclic and finite-character Fourier identities are Lean checked. The standard complex-exponential/norm specialization remains written; concrete linear-algebra/connectivity properties are exact finite computations.

sources.title: Analysis of Absorbing Sets and Fully Absorbing Sets of Array-Based LDPC Codes
sources.date_or_version: IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 56(1), 181–201, January 2010
sources.locator: Section III-C, Lemma 4, printed pp. 187–188 (PDF pp. 7–8)
sources.relationship: Classical diamond/two-triangle structure and exact special-family (4,2) fully absorbing counts; credited ingredients.
sources.comparison_limit: The exponent r*c array family and its special extension multiplicity do not establish the full sparse/two-block polynomial QC-GHP formula. Absorbing and fully absorbing conventions must be kept separate.

sources.title: The Cycle Consistency Matrix Approach to Absorbing Sets in Separable Circulant-Based LDPC Codes
sources.locator: Theorem 1; Section VI, (4,2) CCM and multiplicity
sources.relationship: Classical cycle/check/bit consistency method and explicit (4,2) normal graph.
sources.comparison_limit: Separable-circulant mother/daughter hypotheses, plus non-extensibility in sufficiency, are not a universal incidence-corrected QC-GHP Fourier formula. In a column-weight-three SCB mother/daughter with three retained row groups, each variable has one check in each group. The fixed B^T block in our witness contains a seven-check Fano subsystem whose check co-occurrence graph is K7, so it cannot admit such a three-group partition, even after row/column relabeling.

sources.title: On Characterization of Elementary Trapping Sets of Variable-Regular LDPC Codes
sources.locator: Section III, normal graphs; Sections IV and V-B1
sources.relationship: Normal graph dictionary and cycle expansion enumeration are classical predecessors.
sources.comparison_limit: A normal graph of an already elementary set does not identify all induced diamonds of the unrestricted global variable projection with elementary sets. General enumeration is already known.

sources.title: New Characterization and Efficient Exhaustive Search Algorithm for Elementary Trapping Sets of Variable-Regular LDPC Codes
sources.locator: Dot/path/lollipop characterization and exhaustive search construction

sources.comparison_limit: Does not supply the inspected small-matrix M_j-only QC-GHP count; no claim that the new rooted count is a first exact algorithm.

sources.title: Optimizing quasi-cyclic spatially coupled LDPC codes by eliminating harmful objects
sources.date_or_version: EURASIP Journal on Wireless Communications and Networking 2023, article 67, July 25, 2023
sources.locator: Sections 1.2, 2.1 and 3, especially the declared trapping-set enumeration method
sources.relationship: QC protograph/exponent enumeration and optimization of (4,2) objects are established techniques.
sources.comparison_limit: Uses the prior exhaustive ETS algorithm for trapping-set counts and excludes blocks of circulant weight greater than one (Section 2.1); no inspected full target Fourier formula or equal-M_j obstruction.

sources.title: On a class of column-weight 3 decomposable LDPC codes with the analysis of elementary trapping sets
sources.locator: Definition of decomposability (p586); Section5 pp590–592, Proposition5.5, Theorem3 and proof, Algorithm1, Table5; QC-lift setup Section6
sources.relationship: Classical decomposable-code normal-graph characterization and shape enumeration, including the unique elementary (4,2) shape.
sources.comparison_limit: Three check groups are required, each variable having one check in each. The Fano block in our witness precludes this hypothesis. Algorithm1 enumerates non-isomorphic normal-graph shapes; it is not the inspected incidence-corrected count of embedded sets from arbitrary QC-GHP sockets or a formula in M_j. No matching general corrected Fourier formula identified in the inspected sections.

sources.title: Absorbing Sets in Quantum LDPC Codes
sources.date_or_version: First preprint July 26, 2023; inspected v2 May 10, 2024; journal early access March 3, 2026
sources.locator: Definition 5; Section V-C, Remark 4 and Example 20; Section VI
sources.relationship: Source strict-majority definition and prior propagation of base absorbing sets into ordinary hypergraph products. Constant-label witnesses here are ordinary HGPs, so replication of their base configurations is a classical ingredient, not claimed as a new construction principle.
sources.comparison_limit: The inspected text gives base-matrix characterization/propagation and examples, not an explicit incidence-corrected Fourier formula for nonconstant QC-GHP labels or an M_j-only count. The 2026 journal full text is subscription restricted, so the exact inspected mathematical version is v2 (2024).

sources.title: Trapping Sets of Quantum LDPC Codes
sources.relationship: Prior quantum trapping-set search, constituent-to-HGP replication, and explicit (4,2) enumeration in a 900-qubit example; not claimed as new here.
sources.comparison_limit: Table2 gives 720 elementary (4,2) configurations in one HP example using classical search machinery. The inspected sections do not give our full nonconstant-QC-GHP corrected socket/Fourier formula or equal-M_j obstruction. Harmfulness is decoder dependent; our incidence count does not assert a decoder failure rate.

sources.title: Trapping Set Enumerators for Specific LDPC Codes
sources.date_or_version: Information Theory and Applications Workshop, 2010; author-hosted five-page paper
sources.locator: SectionII graph transformation H-tilde=[H|I] and customized impulse algorithm; SectionsIII–IV and tables
sources.relationship: Earlier general finite-code trapping-set enumerator and concrete (4,2) counts, including QC examples.
sources.comparison_limit: The graph transformation tracks general odd-check counts without imposing elementarity or absorption. Its practical codeword enumeration is explicitly approximate. It is not an inspected exact construction-only corrected Fourier formula, and no priority is claimed for finite-code enumeration.

sources.title: Cospectral Bipartite Graphs with the Same Degree Sequences but with Different Number of Large Cycles
sources.date_or_version: arXiv v1 May31,2019; Graphs and Combinatorics35,1673–1693(2019)
sources.locator: Introduction; SectionIII Theorem2 and degree-preserving switching discussion; SectionVI concluding remarks
sources.relationship: Classical limitations of spectral/degree data for Tanner cycle counts and proposed study of trapping-set changes under cospectral switching.
sources.comparison_limit: SectionVI proposes studying trapping-set distributions under switching. The inspected paper proves cycle-count obstructions, not our elementary (4,2) count at equal full frequency matrices in a QC-GHP/CSS family. Spectral information-loss as a general theme is classical, not claimed as new.

sources.title: Univariate Bicycle Quantum LDPC Codes: Explicit Logical Structure and Distance Bounds
sources.locator: SectionsII-B andIII, Proposition1, defining equations2–3 and Lemma2; targeted text search for absorbing/(4,2)
sources.relationship: Prior Frobenius-coupled GB/UB construction b=a^(2^ell). The 48-qubit pair uses a and its square with a one-sided reciprocal, so this is construction background, not a new code-family claim.
sources.comparison_limit: Their convention is HX=[A|B], whereas the source here uses HX=[A|B^T]; the reciprocal/shift must be accounted for before comparing. Inspected construction sections and targeted text search did not identify a (4,2) incidence/Fourier enumeration or equal-M_j obstruction. No distance theorem from this source is asserted for our witnesses.
